finding.claim: Unauthenticated remote client can enumerate user ids and names for any organization via GET /users?org=<value>; no auth or org-membership check exists on the route.
finding.source: req.query.org (db.js:9), attacker-controlled query string; precondition is only network access to port 3002.
finding.sink: req.pg.query("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1") at db.js:9, with rows returned by res.json(rows) at db.js:10.

trace.note: Route GET /users registered with no auth middleware in chain.
req.query.org bound as $1 (parameterized, no SQLi) and used as the org filter for the query.
All returned id/name rows serialized to the caller.
app.listen(3002) with no host argument binds all interfaces, so the route is network-reachable.

finding.guards_checked: Parameterized query ($1) prevents SQL injection but not cross-org access. No authentication middleware in db.js (no app.use, no route guard). No authorization or org-membership check. No rate limiting. No network restriction in repo. Caveat: req.pg is not defined in this repo; if another deployment file adds auth middleware, the finding changes and was not available to verify. Semgrep was not run (Bash disabled); LLM-native review only.

verdict.guard_found: none. db.js:8 registers GET /users with no auth middleware; db.js:9 parameterizes req.query.org as $1, which stops SQL injection but not cross-org access; db.js:10 returns all rows. No app.use or auth/org check exists in db.js:1-23, and the repo has no other application code that adds one (the only other files are .claude skill docs). db.js:23 binds app.listen(3002) on all interfaces.
verdict.reason: Anonymous network clients can call GET /users with any org value (db.js:8-10) and receive id and name for that org, and no control in db.js:1-23 or elsewhere in the repo blocks it. The caveat is that req.pg is undefined in this repo (db.js:9), so the route cannot run as shipped, and a deployment-level auth layer outside the repo would change the result; that is not visible here.
